audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart read blanket "Skill" on rows 0-3 and row 6 while the content layer and the packet chart both read Lux/Lux/Lux/Lux and Malzahar. Two layers, two answers.
audit.why: Lux outranges him everywhere pre-6 (E 1100, Q 1175 vs Call of the Void 900, Malefic Visions 650). Post-6 Nether Grasp (140/110/80s) and Voidling perma-push flip the side lanes.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side -> Lux, phases[6].side -> Malzahar, matching win[N] already on disk.

audit.why: Lost Chapter, level 6 Final Spark, Luden's and late scaling are all represented in spikes[] with four entries.
audit.corrected: Left the spike timings; corrected the mechanics inside spikes[2] and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Void Shift a "spellshield" that "eats your Q root" and calls Nether Grasp "QSS-immune". Neither is in Riot's text: Void Shift is damage reduction plus crowd-control immunity that ends shortly after he takes damage, and nothing in the kit makes the suppression cleanse-proof. The decisive interaction — Nether Grasp is a channel, so Light Binding cancels it — was never stated.
audit.why: Riot text: Void Shift grants "massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity, lingering for a short period after taking damage". Nether Grasp carries the channel flag: interruptible, any CC cancels it. Call of the Void silences on a flat 6s cooldown.
audit.corrected: Void Shift named correctly as CC immunity you chip off before rooting; Q named as the interrupt for the R channel; the silence window stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that holds real numbers: Nether Grasp 140/110/80s, Call of the Void 6s.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both cooldowns and the interrupt.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to their own titles.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Prismatic Barrier for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp is 140/110/80s and it is a channel — Light Binding (Q) cancels it outright, so bank the root for his R rather than for poke. - Call of the Void silences on a flat 6s cooldown; walk up inside that window, never into it with W already spent.

edits.before: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Lucent Singularity is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s at 1100 range and he farms at 650 with Malefic Visions, so the zone is chip he cannot answer.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Illumination sits on him for seconds, so every spell makes your next auto free — and that damage is what ends Void Shift before you root.

edits.before: Malzahar spends Nether Grasp early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Q is your interrupt — root him as Nether Grasp starts and the channel dies with it.

edits.before: That’s Malzahar’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: A whiffed Q leaves you empty when Call of the Void silences you mid-step.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Final Spark is 60/50/40s and your only screen-range answer to his commit — spend it on a champion, never on a wave you could E-clear.

edits.before: Malzahar wins by landing Nether Grasp, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Malzahar wins by shoving flat with Malefic Visions, walking up behind Void Shift, and suppressing you inside his zone.

edits.after: Malzahar out-scales the sidelanes and objectives: perma-push with Voidlings, Void Shift negating your lockdown until it breaks, and an 80s suppress ult make him the safer scaling pick.

edits.before: His spellshield nullifies your Light Binding and his perma-push plus QSS-proof suppress mean he scales safer; group with your team, poke from fog, and rely on allies to peel his all-in.
edits.after: Void Shift is CC immunity, not a spell shield — chip it off before you root, and QSS or Cleanse still breaks Nether Grasp; group, poke from fog, and let allies peel his all-in.

edits.before: Bait your Q into his passive spellshield, then walk up for R suppress
edits.after: Bait your Q into Void Shift's CC immunity, then walk up for R suppress

notes: Void Shift was described across four fields as a spell shield and the suppression as QSS-immune; both are absent from Riot's text and are now corrected. breakdown.carry and ahead remain structurally templated but the kit gives nothing enemy-specific beyond what the cooldowns and dos/donts now carry, so they were left rather than invented.
